definitions.explanation: A formal document summarizing a company's or organization's financial position, including income, expenses, assets, and liabilities for a given period.

examples.japanese: {決算書|けっさんしょ}を{確認|かくにん}した。
{毎年|まいとし}、{決算書|けっさんしょ}を{作成|さくせい}しなければならない。
examples.english: Financial statements must be prepared every year.

examples.japanese: {決算書|けっさんしょ}を{見|み}れば、{会社|かいしゃ}の{経営状態|けいえいじょうたい}がわかる。
examples.english: By looking at the financial statements, you can understand the company's financial condition.

notes:
A compound of {決算|けっさん} (settlement of accounts) and {書|しょ} (document). An essential business and accounting term. In Japan, companies are required to prepare {決算書|けっさんしょ} at the end of each fiscal year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {決算書|けっさんしょ}を{作成|さくせい}する — to prepare financial statements
- {決算書|けっさんしょ}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する — to submit financial statements
- {決算書|けっさんしょ}を{分析|ぶんせき}する — to analyze financial statements
- {連結|れんけつ}{決算書|けっさんしょ} — consolidated financial statements

RELATED TERMS:
- {決算|けっさん} — settlement of accounts; the broader process of closing books for a period
- {貸借対照表|たいしゃくたいしょうひょう} — balance sheet; one component of a full set of financial statements
- {損益計算書|そんえきけいさんしょ} — income statement; another key financial document
